title: When Can One Neuron Fix Repetition Loops in LLMs?

data.title: When Can One Neuron Fix Repetition Loops in LLMs?
data.research_question: Can targeted static weight edits to a small number of internal components reduce repetition loops in Gemma 4 without retraining, rather than relying on repetition penalties?

models_and_data.quote: The Gemma 4 instruction-tuned models share a reproducible failure: on long factual enumeration prompts,
We use eight enumeration probes: firefly_list, wire_episodes, pokemon_gen1, mcu_films, noble_gases, constellations, us_presidents, and eu_member_states.
For each model variant, the initial loop evaluation consists of these 8 probes × 8 fixed seeds (0-7) × 2 thinking modes (thinking on or off), for 128 generations per model variant.
We generate up to 1536 new tokens with temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95, top_k=64, and no repetition penalty.
For regression checks, we report IFEval (Zhou et al. 2023), TruthfulQA (Lin, Hilton, and Evans 2022), ARC-Easy and ARC-Challenge (Clark et al. 2018), and GSM8K (Cobbe et al. 2021).

We also run three untouched, no-thinking benchmarks that were not used to select variants: HellaSwag (Zellers et al. 2019), WinoGrande (Sakaguchi et al. 2020), and BoolQ (Clark et al. 2019); 500 examples each.

To test whether the approach transfers beyond Gemma, we screened prompts from Antidoom’s released training mixture (Liquid AI 2026b) with Qwen3.5-4B (Qwen Team 2026), then froze a fresh 400-prompt Qwen confirmation set after trigger discovery.
A smaller LFM2.5-1.2B-Thinking experiment (Liquid AI 2026a) provides a second cross-family feasibility result: a 100-neuron edit reduces held-out loops from 4/9 to 1/9.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: No CPU-only runtime, memory, or latency measurements are reported, so the practical cost of the static edits for a CPU lab is unknown.
The paper does not analyze KV-shared layers 15–34, per-layer embeddings, or use activation patching/logit lens/induction-head tracing, so its mechanistic claims do not directly cover those internals.
Evaluation is concentrated on English factual enumeration and a small benchmark set; multilingual behavior, broader code generation, and long-form reasoning remain largely untested.
The intervention search may overfit the small development grid despite held-out seeds; the paper does not report multiple independent selection pipelines or search-run variance.

Static unconditional edits could have unmeasured effects on routing or downstream computation; the paper does not isolate whether loop reduction comes from changed token probabilities, expert routing, or compensatory circuits.
data.relevance_to_lab: Directly relevant: it studies Gemma 4 E2B repetition loops, per-layer ablation/attribution, and MLP-neuron weight edits (L10/L12; L13–L15 signal), with a deterministic loop detector and held-out protocol. It does not cover KV-shared layers 15–34, per-layer embeddings, activation patching, logit lens, induction heads, factual-recall tracing, or CPU feasibility, so it can serve as a behavioral/weight-edit baseline and caution for those internal analyses.

key_results.claim: Across frozen held-out prompts and seeds, the selected edits substantially reduced detected loops.
key_results.quote: Across 384 held-out baseline and 384 paired selected-edit generations, detected loops fall from 46 to 12.

key_results.claim: The strongest held-out reductions occurred for E4B and 31B.
key_results.quote: E4B falls from 18/96 to 2/96 (paired reduction 16.7 pp, 95% bootstrap CI [8.3, 25.0]) and 31B from 13/96 to 3/96 (10.4 pp [4.2, 16.7])

key_results.claim: E2B showed a smaller held-out reduction, while the 26B effect was not distinguishable from zero.
key_results.quote: E2B falls from 6/96 to 1/96 (5.2 pp [0.0, 10.4]), while 26B falls from 9/96 to 6/96 (3.1 pp [−3.1, 9.4]).

key_results.claim: A single sign-inverted E2B neuron eliminated development-grid failures but caused a larger benchmark regression tail.
key_results.numbers: 0/128 failures; L10 neuron 3513; α = −1; benchmark tail about −2.6 pp
key_results.quote: A one-neuron variant that multiplies the L10 neuron 3513 by α = −1 reaches 0/128 failures, but has a worse benchmark tail of about −2.6 pp.

key_results.claim: No statistically detectable regression was found on the separate capability benchmarks.
key_results.numbers: All 12 model–benchmark comparisons: 95% intervals include zero.
key_results.quote: Conservative 95% intervals based on the two reported standard errors include zero in all 12 model–benchmark comparisons (Supplementary Sec. B), so none shows a statistically detectable regression.

key_results.claim: Matched random controls supported selectivity for E4B in both modes, E2B without thinking, and thinking-enabled 31B, but not for 26B or thinking-enabled E2B.
key_results.quote: The selected edit has a lower loop rate than every draw for E4B in both modes, E2B without thinking, and 31B with thinking.

key_results.claim: A sparse L12 sign-inversion edit reduced detector-positive repetition on Qwen3.5-4B under both detectors, although it introduced some new loops.
key_results.numbers: Antidoom detector: 181 to 104 positives; 111 resolved, 34 introduced; exact McNemar p < 10−10. Our detector: 74 to 42; 56 resolved, 24 introduced; p = 0.00045.
key_results.quote: reduces positives from 181 to 104 under Antidoom’s repeated-span detector (111 resolved, 34 introduced; exact McNemar p < 10−10 ) and from 74 to 42 under our detector (56 resolved, 24 introduced; p = 0.00045)

threats_not_stated_by_authors: No CPU-only runtime, memory, or feasibility measurements are reported for backward-pass attribution, model surgery, or generation sweeps, so transfer to the lab's CPU setting is untested.
The paper does not analyze induction heads or copy heads directly, so the edited neurons and routed experts are not localized relative to known induction or copy-suppression circuits.
No logit-lens or per-layer embedding-space readout is used to determine what factual answer, entity, or token representation is present at the localized layers.
The study does not trace factual recall independently, leaving unresolved whether the selected components encode missing facts or only repetition dynamics.
KV-cache sharing is not examined, so the layer-level findings are not validated in a KV-shared architecture.
The effective E2B edits act at L10/L12, whereas the lab focuses on KV-shared layers 15–34; no cross-range replication or layer-index alignment analysis is provided.
The paper does not perform separate thinking-mode-specific localization, leaving open whether the E2B intervention targets the same mechanism when thinking is enabled versus disabled.
data.relevance_to_lab: Directly relevant because the paper studies gemma-4-E2B-it and provides a concrete loop detector, per-layer ablation, gradient-times-activation attribution of MLP down_proj columns, and full-generation causal edits. Its E2B single-token signal is at L13–L15 while the effective edits act earlier at L10/L12, giving the lab a useful comparison point for activation patching, logit-lens, induction-head, and factual-recall traces over layers 15–34. Major gaps are the absence of KV-sharing, per-layer embedding, logit-lens, induction-head, factual-recall, and CPU analyses. The E2B result also needs caution: its one-neuron edit reduced held-out loops only from 6 to 4, and natural termination fell from 90/96 to 81/96.
